import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

I've written the plan for the `,` → `+` switch and submitted it for your approval. Nothing has been changed in either repo yet.

**What it does:** a `,` typed right against a complete marker acts exactly like a typed `+`:
- `@foo:bar,` → `@foo+bar`
- `@foo^bar,` → `@foo+bar`

Today bob leaves that `,` alone, and the marker then fails to parse ("invalid block ID"), so nothing useful is lost. Undo in the Mac app still gives you back the literal `,`.

**It only goes one way.** `.` toggles `:` ↔ `^`, but `,` can't switch back from `+`. That's because `@foo+bar,` already means "start the next parent task" and becomes `@foo+bar +`. That stays as it is, and typing `,` twice now takes you from `@foo:bar` to `@foo+bar` to `@foo+bar +`. To get from `+` back to `:` or `^`, type `:` or `^` as today.

**The plan** (one coding agent, small size):
- **bob-cli:** treat a glued `,` as `+` inside the existing separator switch. It then automatically works everywhere `+` already does: transfer lines (`@inbox:bench, > @db`), merge sources (`< @work:a,`), and runs of several `@route+id` markers on one line.
- **Unchanged:** after a sealed project-note marker (`@route:id@,`) the `,` stays literal, as `+` does. Bullet task IDs (`- Task :id,`) are untouched because they have no `+` form.
- **Mac app:** typing in the editor already sends `,` to bob, so only the New ID picker needs a change. Your screenshot case types the ID into that picker, so `,` gets added to its short list of keys that are sent to bob.
- **Tests and docs:** two existing Rust test entries say `@cash:goog-exit,` stays literal; the plan moves them into the new tests. It also adds CLI and Swift tests and updates help text and docs in both repos.
- **Checks:** `just check` and `just docs-check` in bob-cli. On the Mac side, the app's own code only compiles on macOS, so the agent runs it through macOS CI (`scripts/dev/macos-ci-check`). Last time the `mac` host couldn't be reached over SSH.

**Decision for you when you review:**
- **Updating the Capture Alias glossary note** to mention the `,` switch next to the `.` toggle: off by default, because the note isn't wrong without it. You turned the matching option on last time, so flip it on if you want the same here.
